mula_devanagari: ऋषिभिर् बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर् विविधैः पृथक् | ब्रह्म-सूत्र-पदैश् चैव हेतुमद्भिर् विनिश्चितैः
mula_iast: ṛṣibhir bahudhā gītaṃ chandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛthak | brahma-sūtra-padaiś caiva hetumadbhir viniścitaiḥ
jayatirtha_prameyadipika: ।।13.5।।ब्रह्मणः सूचकानि वाक्यानि ब्रह्मसूत्राणि (शं.) इति कश्चित्। ततश्च छन्दसामृषिवाक्यानां च तथात्वात् ऋषिभिरित्यादिकं वृथा स्यादित्यतो रूढिमाश्रित्याह -- ब्रह्मे ति।

current_dvaita_rendering.english: The brahma-sūtra here are the śārīraka (the sūtra on the embodied self, the Vedānta-sūtra of Bādarāyaṇa).
current_dvaita_rendering.divergence_note: THIN. Madhva (his 13.5) glosses only one word, but it is a pointed one: 'brahma-sūtra' means the śārīraka-sūtra, the text of Bādarāyaṇa, against the Advaita reading of it as Upaniṣad sentences. Nothing is said about the ṛṣi, the chandas, or 'hetumat'.

current_dvaita_everyday: Madhva glosses one word, and uses it to say exactly which text is meant. A lawyer or a contract manager knows the value of that habit: when someone says 'the agreement says', ask which agreement and which clause. Nothing else in this verse is commented on.

other_schools_english.advaita: The true nature of field and knower has been sung in many ways by the ṛṣi (seers), Vasiṣṭha and others, and separately, with discrimination, by the many kinds of chandas (sacred meters of the Veda), the Ṛk and the rest. It has been sung too by the brahma-sūtra-pada: 'brahma-sūtra' are the sentences that point to Brahman, and 'pada' are those by which it is reached and known, such as 'let one meditate on it as the self alone'; reasoned, and settled, producing conviction without doubt.
other_schools_english.viśiṣṭādvaita: This true nature of field and knower has been sung in many ways by ṛṣi (seers) such as Parāśara, who teaches that the self is pure, imperishable, beyond prakṛti, and asks 'is the head you, is the belly you? Ask, who am I', and the Mahābhārata adds that senses, mind and both field and knower are Vāsudeva-ātmaka (having Vāsudeva as their self). The four Veda sing them apart: the Taittirīya names the body made of food, then within it the knower made of understanding, and within the knower the ānandamaya (self made of bliss), the supreme self as the knower's inner self. And the śārīraka-sūtra, reasoned and conclusive, settle the field in 'na viyad aśruteḥ', the knower in 'nātmā aśruteḥ' and 'jño 'ta eva', and the knower's being impelled by the Lord in 'parāt tu tac chruteḥ': hear it now from me briefly and clearly.
other_schools_english.śuddhādvaita: The form of the knower has been sung in many ways, because a meaning scattered across many teachings cannot be gathered up by any single one: by the chandas (hymns of the Veda) it is taught as the object of meditation and fixing of mind, as the Vairāja cosmic form, as the deities worshipped in various sacrifices; and separately by the brahma-sūtra-pada composed by Vyāsa, which string together the essence of the meaning of the Veda and are therefore settled, rich in reasons, each hetu (reason) a proving text such as 'tat tu samanvayāt'. All of this I have sung in many ways, and now I gather its essence, its fruit, and tell it to you.
other_schools_english.bhakti: By ṛṣi such as Vasiṣṭha in the yoga texts it is set out many ways as an object of meditation and concentration in the Vairāja form; by the many Veda on daily, occasional and desire-driven rites as the various deities to be worshipped; by brahma-sūtra, sentences such as 'from which these beings are born' that point to Brahman by its marks, and by pada, sentences such as 'Brahman is truth, knowledge, the infinite' that reach Brahman in its own nature. These are hetumat (backed by reasons), as 'how could being come from non-being?' and 'who would breathe, if this bliss were not in space?', and viniścita (settled), because their opening and close agree; what they say at length, hard to gather, I will tell you briefly. Or else brahma-sūtra means the sūtra beginning 'athāto brahma-jijñāsā', with reasons such as 'īkṣater nāśabdam'.
other_schools_english.advaita-bhakti: To win the listener over by praise: it has been sung many ways by ṛṣi such as Vasiṣṭha in the yoga texts as the object of fixing and meditating, which shows it is taught by the dharma-śāstra (law and ethics); by the chandas, the mantra and brāhmaṇa on daily, occasional and desired rites, separately and with discrimination, which shows it is taught by the karma-kāṇḍa (ritual portion); and by brahma-sūtra and pada, the Upaniṣad sentences pointing to Brahman by its marks and by its nature, backed by reasons such as 'how could being come from non-being?' and settled by the agreement of opening and close, which shows it is taught by the jñāna-kāṇḍa (knowledge portion). What all these have said at great length I will tell you in brief. Or take it as one compound: the sūtra of vidyā, such as 'let one meditate on it as the self', and the sūtra of avidyā, such as 'he does not know, he is like a beast'.
